Definition: from a compound of G1 (as a negative particle) and the base of G4198; to have no way out, i.e. be at a loss (mentally):-- (stand in) doubt, be perplexed.
BiblicalUsage: To have no way out, to be at a loss. The women at the tomb were much perplexed in Luke 24:4, and two men stood by them in shining garments; the disciples looked one on another in John 13:22, doubting of whom He spake. Herod heard John gladly in Mark 6:20, yet was perplexed by him, and Paul tells the Galatians in Galatians 4:20 that he stands in doubt of them.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe perplexity is honest ground, and the Bible does not scold it. The women were perplexed and then saw angels; the disciples doubted and then heard the truth; Herod was perplexed and would not act; Paul stood in doubt and wrote to win them back. Being at a loss is not the sin — staying there, when the way out has been shown, is.
